summary: I audited the three rig runs independently from the raw points files and reproduced the logged numbers. My standalone copy of the rig's P_max rule gives the logged raw argmax exactly for all 42 set points: power, current, voltage, step count, last current and the stopped_by text. It gives the logged parabolic fit to within 0.00006 W (0.14%) for Ra40 and Ra80, and it produces the Ra20 fit that was never logged. On the fit basis, the pairwise LEVELs (geometric mean over 14 set points, t-based 95% CI) are: Ra40/Ra20 +8.74% [+6.11, +11.44], Ra80/Ra20 +13.67% [+9.95, +17.52], Ra80/Ra40 +4.53% [+2.06, +7.06]. On the raw basis they are +8.41%, +13.73% and +4.91%. The 4-21 rpm "slip" in Ra20 does not come from the fan running slow. Ra20's fan_rpm_actual is the drive's output frequency multiplied by 29.5 rpm/Hz. All 14 values sit on that 2.95-rpm grid; the chance of that happening at random is 2.6e-7. Ra80 and Ra40 read the drive's own SPEED parameter (0102), which the code has used since commit 465f286 on 25 Aug. Parameter 5310 was 103 both before and after that change. Motor current is the same across runs to within 0.1 A, which also argues against a real slowdown. My recommendation is to use v = 0.02132*fan_rpm_cmd - 0.424 for every run, in plots and in tables. Most of the rougher blades' extra power shows up as higher light-load voltage and Voc: Voc is +4.1% (Ra40) and +6.4% (Ra80) higher than Ra20 at all 14 set points. Apparent internal resistance shows no resolvable change (-0.7% [-2.7, +1.4] and -0.4% [-2.2, +1.5]). Since 2*dlnVoc accounts for 92-97% of dlnP, the rougher rotors were turning faster at light load. That fits an aerodynamic cause, but a stronger wind on the later test days cannot be excluded, because no run measured wind independently. The power ordering follows Ra (13/14 set points), not test date (1/14). Ra20, however, is also the first run and the only one taken before the software and firmware changes of 22-26 Aug. Ra40's reed-switch turbine_rpm cannot be used for anything.
key_findings: P_max rule (src/peak_finder.py, unchanged since commit 7d4dba4; called by sweep_core.measure_point). RAW: the argmax of V*I over ramp dwells, excluding the first (floor) dwell and any 'bad' dwell; a later sample must be strictly greater to replace the peak. FIT (PeakResult.refine, span=2): take the tracking dwells with I>0 (floor dwell included), find the first max-watts index k, and fit a least-squares quadratic W(I) in measured current (Cramer's rule) through pts[k-2..k+2]. It falls back to raw if there are fewer than 5 points, the window has fewer than 3, the determinant is below 1e-18, a2>=0 (not concave), or the vertex lies outside [window[0].I, window[-1].I].

My standalone re-implementation gives the logged raw p/i/v with 0 discrepancy at 42/42 set points. Steps and i_last also match 42/42, and the power-rolloff stop replay reproduces every stopped_by string (14/14 per run). Logged fit vs my recompute: Ra40 max |dP| 0.00006 W (0.137%, at 1500), Ra80 0.00006 W (0.063%, at 1800). That is 4-dp rounding in the points files; by Monte Carlo, rounding moves the Ra20 fit by at most a 0.13% half-width.
The fit falls back to raw at two set points: Ra20 at 700 (vertex outside the window), which is new, and Ra40 at 600 (not concave), which matches the logged value. All other fits use 5 points.

Fan speed: Ra20's summary fan_rpm_actual is 4-21 rpm below command (10 distinct values). All 14 values equal round(k*2.95), i.e. PMC f2 (output Hz/10) * 295: output frequency in 0.1 Hz steps times 29.5 rpm/Hz. At a 4-pole motor's 30 rpm/Hz, that frequency puts synchronous speed 3.1-10.5 rpm above the command, which is ordinary slip with the shaft at the set point. The 29.5 factor bakes rated slip (sync/60) into every reading. Ra40 and Ra80 read drive parameter 0102 SPEED over RD (commit 465f286, 25 Aug 14:01): 0/+1 rpm in the summaries, -2..+1 rpm in the Ra40 trace.

Parameter 5310 = 103 in the 25 Aug 13:31 drive snapshot (before Ra80) and in the Ra40 header. The register mapping never changed. The Ra40 header's drive_actual_signals describes register 40005, but the fan_rpm_actual column bypasses that register.

Motor current at the same commanded speed agrees across runs to within +/-0.1 A at every set point. If Ra20's fan had really been 16-21 rpm slow at 1600-1800, the within-run slope predicts 0.16-0.19 A less current. Ra20 reads 11.9/12.7/13.6 A against Ra80's 11.8/12.7/13.6 A.

Wind columns: summary wind_mps = f(actual rpm at the end of settle); points wind_mps = f(commanded rpm); the header wind_mps is the first set point only. Ra20's summary wind is 0.71-1.20% (mean 1.03%) below commanded-rpm wind, which is 2.7-4.7% in power at n=3.77 (mean 3.96%). Ra40 and Ra80 summary wind is within -0.02..+0.10% of it. Plotting Ra20 on its summary wind shrinks the matched-wind Ra40/Ra20 gap from +8.44% to +4.51%, and Ra80/Ra20 from +13.37% to +9.26% (13 common set points).

Recommendation: use one wind definition everywhere, v = 0.02132*fan_rpm_cmd - 0.424 (the points files' wind_mps). The calibration (Test 1, 13 Feb 2026) was fitted against round set-point rpm, and the 0102 readback equals the set point to within about 1 rpm.

Thevenin analysis (my mirror matches the repo's generator_model.py at 42/42 set points). Rougher blades show higher light-load voltage at an identical 1-10 mA floor current: Ra40/Ra20 +3.92% [+2.88, +4.96], Ra80/Ra20 +6.29% [+4.46, +8.15] (14/14 each), Ra80/Ra40 +2.29% [+0.71, +3.88] (11/14). Voc: +4.08%, +6.40%, +2.23%. Apparent R_int: -0.66% [-2.66, +1.38], -0.35% [-2.16, +1.49], +0.31% [-1.44, +2.09], all indistinguishable from zero. Mean dlnP_fit = 2dlnVoc + (-dlnR): Ra40/Ra20 8.38 = 8.00 + 0.66; Ra80/Ra20 12.81 = 12.42 + 0.36; Ra80/Ra40 4.43 = 4.41 - 0.31 (log-%). A fit using only pre-peak points gives the same split.

Reading of the Thevenin result: the extra power comes through Voc, i.e. faster rotor speed at light load, not through lower resistance. That fits an aerodynamic effect. The rig cannot tell it apart from a stronger wind on the later days: there is no independent wind measurement, and ambient air was recorded only for Ra40, uncalibrated. A model-dependent check argues against a pure wind offset for Ra80/Ra20. Under R ~ v^-0.791, the offset implied by Voc would lower R by 3.28%; the observed -0.36% has a CI of [-2.19, +1.48] that excludes it. For Ra40/Ra20 the test does not decide (predicted -2.11%, observed -0.66% [-2.70, +1.37]).

Runs: Ra80 first-to-last dwell 15:24:10-15:32:01 on 26 Aug (471.0 s, 352 dwells). Ra40 15:04:49-15:12:46 on 1 Sep (477.5 s, 352 dwells; trace 15:04:25-15:12:50). Ra20 has 336 dwells with no timestamps or clock. All 42 set points are clean=1 and limited_by=power-rolloff, with 0 tracking=0 rows and 0 notes. Median dwell period is 1.055 s, with 7.4-11.8 s gaps between set points. In both timestamped runs the header 'clock' is 8.0 s after the last dwell, i.e. end of run, although its note says 'run start'.

Test order vs Ra: the raw power ordering Ra20<Ra40<Ra80 holds at 13/14 set points (not at 700). The test-date ordering Ra20<Ra80<Ra40 holds at 1/14 (700 only). Mean ranks: Ra20 1.00, Ra80 2.93, Ra40 2.07. So the result does not track test order monotonically. Ra20, however, is confounded: it is the first run, uses pre-git code, and was taken before the 22-26 Aug firmware and software changes. Ra40 is the only run with a rotor magnet on record.

Ra40 turbine_rpm cannot be used. Within a set point the coefficient of variation is 21.8-61.3% (median 33.6%) and max/min is 2.6-271x. Adjacent-dwell jumps have a median of 26% and a 90th percentile of 104%. Rotor rpm falls significantly with load at only 2/14 set points. The implied light-load 'generator constant' V/rpm varies 10.1x (0.314-3.187 mV/rpm). The median reed rpm rises only 7717 to 10436 from fan 500 to 1600, then drops to 8199 at 1800, while light-load voltage rises 8.1x. Summary TSR runs 0.28-8.60 and is not monotonic.

anomalies.issue: Ra20 summary fan_rpm_actual and wind_mps are output frequency x 29.5 rpm/Hz, not shaft speed. The repo's docs call the Ra20 summary wind 'physically correct'.
anomalies.evidence: All 14 Ra20 summary actuals equal round(k*2.95) (chance 2.6e-7); Ra40 points are on that grid at chance level (10/29) and Ra80 likewise (4/14). The PMC firmware reads 40005 (OUTPUT FREQ) /100 as f2, and the pre-25-Aug transport returned f2*295. Commit 465f286 switched to par 0102 SPEED. Implied synchronous speed is 3-10.5 rpm above command, i.e. normal slip. Motor current is equal across runs to within 0.1 A. docs/09_results.md (~line 197) says '37.50 is the physically correct figure'.

Use wind from commanded rpm for all runs, or the Ra20 curve shifts ~1% left and the matched-wind roughness gap shrinks by ~4 points (Ra40/Ra20 +8.44% to +4.51%). ### 2. P_max rule and recompute

**Source.** `src/peak_finder.py`, unchanged since 7d4dba4 (22 Aug), called from `sweep_core.measure_point` with operate_frac=0.

- **RAW** is the argmax of V·I over ramp dwells. The first (floor) dwell is excluded, and so is any bad dwell (collapsed, lost tracking, or under v_floor). A later sample must be strictly greater to replace the peak.
- **FIT** (`refine(span=2)`) uses the tracking dwells with I>0, including the floor dwell. It finds the first max-watts index k and fits an ordinary least-squares quadratic W(I) in measured current, solved by Cramer's rule, through pts[k-2..k+2]. i_fit = -a1/2a2 and p_fit = W(i_fit).
- **Fallback to raw** happens if there are fewer than 5 points, the window has fewer than 3, |det| < 1e-18, a2 >= 0, or the vertex lies outside [window[0].I, window[-1].I].
- `compare_blades.py` uses the fit only when both runs have it, so every Ra20 comparison so far has been raw.

Pairing on commanded rpm is unaffected.

**Recommendation.** Use one definition in both plots and tables: v = 0.02132·fan_rpm_cmd - 0.424, which is the points files' wind_mps. The calibration (Test 1, 13 Feb) was fitted against set-point rpm.

**Model check.** Voc²/4R reproduces p_fit to a mean of -0.45%, -0.16% and -0.52% by run, and to within ±4.8% at every set point.

**What drives the difference.** It comes through Voc, not R: 92% (Ra40/Ra20) and 97% (Ra80/Ra20) of the log-power gain. At 1-10 mA the I·R drop is 1.5-3% of V and the same across blades. With the same generator, a higher V_light means the rougher rotors turned about 3.9% (Ra40) and 6.3% (Ra80) faster at light load at the same commanded fan speed. Apparent R includes rotor droop (docs/11), so an unchanged R means the combined electrical-plus-droop slope did not change.

**Alternative: a stronger wind on later days.** This cannot be excluded, because no run measured wind independently. Density differences alone would move P_max but, to first order, not light-load speed. A model-dependent check uses the within-run R ~ v^-0.791. Under that model, the wind offset implied by Voc predicts dlnR of -2.11% for Ra40/Ra20; the observed -0.66% [-2.70, +1.37] does not decide. For Ra80/Ra20 it predicts -3.28%, and the observed -0.36% [-2.19, +1.48] excludes that.
